name: Atacama Desert, Chile
why: One of the driest places on Earth, with soil chemistry and life limits studied as a Mars analog.
breaks_down: Far warmer than the lunar poles, 1 g gravity, thick atmosphere.

name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island, Canada
why: Polar desert impact crater used for rover and human-operations field tests.
breaks_down: Carbonate target rock, not basalt; liquid water and some life present in summer.

name: Death Valley, USA
why: Arid basin with alluvial fans, evaporites and large temperature swings.
breaks_down: Much hotter and denser air than Mars; no permafrost or ice.

name: Askja and Highlands lava fields, Iceland
why: Fresh basaltic terrain with volcano-ice interaction, used for Apollo and rover training.
breaks_down: Wetter and colder than Mars; vegetation and rain are present.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica
why: Cold hyperarid ice-free valleys with ground ice, a classic Mars analog.
breaks_down: Thicker atmosphere and higher pressure; local meltwater exists.

name: Lava Beds National Monument, USA
why: Basaltic lava tube field, useful for studying subsurface shelter and exploration.
breaks_down: Tubes are much smaller than those seen on the Moon and Mars.

name: Craters of the Moon, Idaho, USA
why: Young rugged basalt flows and lava tubes, used for astronaut field training.
breaks_down: Sagebrush cover and seasonal moisture; far less extreme temperatures.

name: Mauna Kea, Hawaii, USA
why: Basaltic cinder terrain used for regolith and ISRU technology tests.
breaks_down: Humid maritime climate below the summit; 1 g and thick air.

name: Danakil Depression, Ethiopia
why: Hot basaltic basin with acid brine pools, a less-studied analog for ancient Mars chemistry.
breaks_down: Extreme heat, not cold; access and safety are difficult.

name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
why: Huge flat salt crust, useful for testing landing, rover navigation and calibration.
breaks_down: Too flat to represent crater or mountain terrain; seasonal water.

name: Dasht-e Lut, Iran
why: Extremely hot, dry, vegetation-free desert with wind-sculpted ridges (yardangs).
breaks_down: Heat extremes and field access limit practical testing.

name: Adventdalen, Svalbard, Norway
why: Permafrost valley with pingos and patterned ground, an analog for Martian ground ice.
breaks_down: Wetter and vegetated; strong marine influence.

name: Meteor Crater, Arizona, USA
why: Young, well-preserved simple impact crater used for astronaut crater training.
breaks_down: Sedimentary target rock; far warmer than polar lunar craters.

name: Ries Crater, Germany
why: Eroded complex impact structure with well-studied breccias, used in Apollo training.
breaks_down: Heavily vegetated and eroded; temperate climate.

name: Pinacate volcanic field, Mexico
why: Arid basaltic field with maar craters and dunes, a combined volcanic and desert analog.
breaks_down: Hot summers and sparse desert plants; no polar cold.

name: Teide volcanic area, Tenerife, Spain
why: High-altitude volcanic terrain and lava tubes, used in ESA analog campaigns.
breaks_down: Island climate and tourism limit access; moderate temperatures.

name: Tibesti volcanic massif, Chad
why: Hyperarid volcanic highland, a little-studied combination of dryness and volcanism.
breaks_down: Remote and unsafe to reach, which limits practical use.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
why: Dry sandstone canyons and dunes, used as a Mars film and analog location.
breaks_down: Sandstone not basalt; warm and tourist-visited.

name: Taklamakan Desert, China
why: Huge dune sea with large day-night swings, useful for dust and aeolian studies.
breaks_down: Sand dunes, not rocky or cratered terrain.

name: Ojos del Salado high Andes, Chile
why: Very high, cold, dry volcanic terrain with low air pressure and strong UV.
breaks_down: Still much thicker air than Mars; altitude hazards for crews.

name: Kangerlussuaq ice margin, Greenland
why: Ice sheet margin with cold dry katabatic winds, useful for polar ice and logistics tests.
breaks_down: Wetter than the poles of the Moon; ice sheet, not buried ice.

name: Rio Tinto, Spain
why: Acidic river with iron minerals and extremophiles, a Mars mineralogy and habitability analog.
breaks_down: Wet, vegetated, mild climate; analogous only for chemistry.
